name: Breri
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only Z'graggen 1969 comparative wordlist material on Glottolog; no phonology/grammar located online (SIL/OLAC blocked or empty).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page brer1240 (Breri) and romk1240 (Romkun), 2026-09-17.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Alternative names Breri, Kuanga; AES 'shifting'. References listed: Z'graggen 1969 (subclassification) and Campbell et al. 2022 (ELCat). Descriptive refs (via our source list): Tousch 2016 only.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. & J. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1, 731-763. Pacific Linguistics C-38 (handle 1885/252975).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Breri named once, in the Tamolan family listing (Midsivindi, Akrukay, Breri, Romkun, Kominimung, Igana). Zero 'stress'/'accent' hits in the chapter text layer.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU (handle 1885/146484).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Breri (M8) appears only in language/village lists and the Rao-Breri census area (pop. 1,072 in 1972). No 'stress'/'accent' hits.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU (handle 1885/146580).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Same wording as the thesis, p. 6: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Breri §2.23.22.14 and Tamolan typology §2.23.22.3 repeat the 1969 text (voiced/voiceless vocoids; Romkun possibly tonal). Nothing on Breri stress; 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere else.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University (ANU Open Research handle 1885/130077).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey-wide only: p. 13 (text-layer page marker) 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Breri entry §2.23.22.14 (p. 153) gives villages, population 720, Kasprus wordlist and Stanhope 1968 medical terms only; Tamolan typological characteristics (pp. 154-155): 'Breri seems to have voiced and voiceless vocoids', 'Romkun is possibly tonal'. No Breri stress statement.

sources.citation: Tousch, André. 2016. Kwanga grammar: Tentative grammar conclusions for the Kwanga language. Ms., 59 pp. SIL Papua New Guinea.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked; the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.note: The only grammar sketch of Breri that exists (Glottolog's sole descriptive ref); SIL-PNG 'tentative grammar conclusions' documents sometimes open with a phonology/orthography note that would state stress placement. Held by Hammarström as a non-shareable file; not in SIL's archive listing.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no library e-access found (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Standard survey of Ramu-family phonology and typology; may carry a family-level statement on stress/tone in the Tamolan (Goam) languages that would situate Breri, though a Breri-specific statement is unlikely.

sources.citation: Joseph (researcher/recorder). 2016. 'Iski request for a linguist' 1, 2, 4. Endangered Languages Archive (ELAR), SOAS; OLAC oai:soas.ac.uk:MPI1226417, MPI1226369, MPI1226374.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only known audio of Breri-Romkun ('Iski'); no description, but usable for an instrumental check of prominence if a written statement never surfaces.

sources.citation: Tousch, André. 2013. Iski word lists. Ms., 12 pp. (Breri villages Oguru, Lembubu, Kwanga, Misingi; Romkun villages Romakun, Yamu 2; Kominimung; Igana).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Recent SIL survey wordlists across Breri and Romkun villages; if transcribed with stress marks they would give the first evidence of Breri stress placement.

sources.citation: Easton, Catherine, Nafian Saremo, Roman Saremo, Noel Diru, Martin Barang, Yong Lam Liaw & Barbara Hodgkinson. 2001. Breri (Mbñioŋko, Kwanga) Alphabet Development Worksheet. SIL International / SIL PNG. OLAC oai:sil.org:70465.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL-PNG alphabet-design workshop worksheets carry the participants' phonological analysis (phoneme chart, syllable patterns, and usually a suprasegmentals/stress or tone line); it is the only phonology-oriented record for brq in OLAC. Companion primer 'Kvoŋko Uwu Irkŋɨ' (oai:sil.org:70493).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1974. Ramu comparative wordlist. St. Augustin: Anthropos Institute, 441 pp. (and 1972 Alexishafen edition, iii+380 pp.).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Largest Breri/Romkun lexical record (Z'graggen's own transcriptions); worth checking whether stress was marked there, though his 1969/1971 survey says it was omitted for want of an established pattern.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1972. Comparative wordlist of the Ramu language group, New Guinea. Alexishafen: Anthropos Institute, iii+380 pp; and 1974. Ramu comparative wordlist. St. Augustin: Anthropos Institute, 441 pp. (Glottolog refs 306728, 590199; language code includes Breri [brq], Romkun [rmk]).
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Wordlists, not opened; the companion 1969/1971 survey states stress marking was omitted, so these are unlikely to mark it.
